No test spec — `run.mjs` is just the agent harness (note `tsconfig.json` excludes `EVAL.tsx`, so verification is added later). 

One important constraint shapes the design: an inline `'use server'` action **cannot** live in a Client Component — Next.js rejects that outright. So the "inline server action defined directly in ContactForm.tsx" requirement means `ContactForm` must stay a Server Component, following the same module-scope pattern already in `page.tsx`.

events.content:
Done. The working tree is back to just my intended change (`package.json`/`package-lock.json` were already modified before I started).

## What I implemented

`app/ContactForm.tsx:1` — a Server Component with a colocated inline server action:

```tsx
async function saveContactMessage(formData: FormData) {
  'use server'
  const name = formData.get('name') as string
  const email = formData.get('email') as string
  const message = formData.get('message') as string

  if (!name?.trim() || !email?.trim() || !message?.trim()) { /* reject */ }
  // Simulate saving the contact message
}
```

The form renders `name`, `email` (type=email), and a `message` textarea, wired via `<form action={saveContactMessage}>`. I followed the module-scope inline `'use server'` pattern already established in `app/page.tsx:4` rather than inventing a new one.

## Verification

Typecheck and production build both pass (`tsc --noEmit` exit 0, `next build` exit 0). I also ran the built server and POSTed to the action directly to exercise the real code path, not just compilation:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| All three fields present | `Saving contact message: { name: 'Ada', email: 'ada@example.com', message: 'Hello there' }` |
| `message` field absent | Rejected — `{ name: true, email: true, message: false }` |
| Whitespace-only `name` | Rejected — `{ name: false, email: true, message: true }` |

The rendered HTML confirms the inline action got its own distinct `$ACTION_ID_40517857a5…`, separate from `updateProfile`'s — so it's genuinely registered as an independent server action.

Two notes worth flagging:

- **The `as string` cast is a lie about nullability**, which is why the guard uses `!name?.trim()` rather than `!name.trim()`. Test case 2 above (absent field → `null`) would throw a TypeError on the un-chained version. I kept the cast to match the surrounding codebase idiom but made the guard null-safe.
- **Validation failures currently only log server-side** and can't be shown in the UI. This is a direct consequence of the inline-action requirement: surfacing errors to the user needs `useActionState`, which requires `'use client'` — and Next.js explicitly forbids inline `'use server'` actions in Client Components. If you want visible error messages, the action has to move into its own `'use server'` file so `ContactForm` can become a client component. Happy to make that change if you'd prefer the better UX over the inline constraint.
